policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV asks 'Am I not free? am I not an apostle?' with free before apostle, which excludes r02's inverted order (apostle first). Between r00-base and r01 the only difference is the Greek question mark after ἐλεύθερος; ASV's two successive English questions is ordinary punctuation of a rhetorical pair and does not settle an editorial mark in the Greek.
ASV reads 'have I not seen Jesus our Lord?' with no 'Christ'; the added Χριστόν of r01 is unrepresented.

'the seal of mine apostleship' renders a possessive equally well from μου τῆς ἀποστολῆς or τῆς ἐμῆς ἀποστολῆς; ASV has no device that distinguishes the enclitic genitive from the possessive adjective, and no note is attached.
Word order only: 'My defence ... is this' is the same English for ἐστιν αὕτη and αὕτη ἐστιν. Nothing in ASV distinguishes them.
πεῖν and πιεῖν are orthographic variants of the same aorist infinitive; 'to drink' cannot distinguish them.
The added article τοῦ before μὴ ἐργάζεσθαι is an articular-infinitive variant with no English exponent; 'a right to forbear working' fits either.

ASV renders the vineyard clause with a bare object, 'eateth not the fruit thereof', against the partitive of the next clause, 'eateth not of the milk of the flock'. That contrast reproduces accusative τὸν καρπόν beside ἐκ τοῦ γάλακτος; r01's ἐκ τοῦ καρποῦ would have produced 'of the fruit' in the same breath.
ASV begins the third clause 'or who feedeth a flock'; the conjunction 'or' represents ἤ, which only r01 has.

All three readings yield a negative rhetorical question with the law as subject; ASV's 'or saith not the law also the same?' represents καί ('also') and the negative alike whether the negative stands as οὐ before λέγει or as οὐχί before καί. Word order and the placement of the negative leave no English trace here.
κημώσεις and φιμώσεις are both 'muzzle'; ASV's 'Thou shalt not muzzle the ox' fits either, and the only note is the Deut. 25:4 cross-reference, which is not a textual note.

Word order only: 'he that ploweth ought to plow in hope' is the same for ὀφείλει ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι and ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι ὀφείλει. The verse's only note, 'Or, altogether', is an alternative_rendering on πάντως and cannot decide a reading.

ASV's thresher clause is 'to thresh in hope of partaking' — a single prepositional phrase with an articular infinitive, matching ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν. r01's τῆς ἐλπίδος αὐτοῦ μετέχειν ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι would require 'to partake of his hope' and a second 'in hope', neither of which ASV has.
Word order only; 'this right over you' renders either ὑμῶν ἐξουσίας or ἐξουσίας ὑμῶν. The note is a cross-reference to the marginal note on 4:15, not a textual note on this unit.
Word order only: 'no hindrance' represents τινα ἐγκοπήν under the negative in either order.
ASV 'eat of the things of the temple'; the presence or absence of the article τά before ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ leaves no distinguishing mark in this English, which supplies 'the things' either way.
παρεδρεύοντες and προσεδρεύοντες are synonyms both rendered 'they that wait upon the altar'; ASV does not distinguish the compound.
ASV has the English perfect, 'But I have used none of these things', matching the perfect κέχρημαι; r01's aorist ἐχρησάμην would have given ASV's usual simple past ('I used none').

ASV completes the comparison as a clause: 'for it were good for me rather to die, than that any man should make my glorying void'. 'than that any man should' renders ἤ ... ἵνα τις κενώσῃ. The base reading is the abrupt independent future οὐδεὶς κενώσει, which would give 'no man shall make my glorying void' as a separate sentence, not the subordinate clause ASV prints.
ASV opens the verse 'For if I preach the gospel', rendering γάρ; r01's δέ would be 'But/And'. The two notes are cross-references to 1:17, not textual notes.
Aorist εὐαγγελίσωμαι against present εὐαγγελίζωμαι in a conditional subjunctive; ASV's 'if I preach the gospel' does not mark the aspect.
'What then is my reward?' is the natural English for both the genitive μού and the dative μοί of advantage; ASV supplies the possessive 'my' either way and attaches no textual note here.
ASV reads 'I may make the gospel without charge' with no qualifier; r01's added τοῦ Χριστοῦ ('the gospel of Christ') is unrepresented.
ASV prints the clause 'not being myself under the law' between 'as under the law' and 'that I might gain them that are under the law', word for word μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον. r01 omits it.
ASV renders 'not being without law to God' with the same 'to' it uses for 'under law to Christ'; that flat rendering does not distinguish genitive θεοῦ from dative θεῷ.
'under law to Christ' renders ἔννομος Χριστοῦ and ἔννομος Χριστῷ alike; ASV marks no case distinction here.
κερδάνω and κερδήσω are alternative aorist subjunctive forms of the same verb; 'that I might gain' fits either.
'them that are without law' supplies an English relative for ἀνόμους with or without the article τούς; ASV gives no signal of the article.

ASV reads 'To the weak I became weak', without the 'as' it uses throughout the surrounding series ('as a Jew', 'as under the law', 'as without law'). The absence of that comparative just where the parallel would invite it answers to the base reading without ὡς.
'I am become all things to all men' renders πάντα with or without the article τά; ASV does not distinguish articular τὰ πάντα from bare πάντα.
ASV reads 'And I do all things for the gospel's sake' — a plural object, πάντα; r01's Τοῦτο would give the singular 'this I do'.
